candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS Tallink Grupp’s financial performance weakened in 2025 amid low consumer and business confidence, economic challenges in its core markets and heightened geopolitical tensions.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue declined 2.6% to EUR 765.3 million from EUR 785.8 million in 2024, while EBITDA fell 25.7% to EUR 130.1 million from EUR 175.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Net profit decreased 57.1% to EUR 17.3 million, or EUR 0.023 per share, compared with EUR 40.3 million, or EUR 0.054 per share, in the previous year.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Accordingly, the EBITDA margin fell from 22.3% to 17.0% and the net profit margin from 5.1% to 2.3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Passenger volumes were broadly stable, with 5.5 million passengers carried, down 0.9%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Cargo volumes declined more sharply, falling 19.2% to 245,004 units, while passenger vehicles decreased 2.2% to 760,473.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Estonia-Finland passenger numbers increased 1.8%, supporting a EUR 1.7 million increase in route revenue to EUR 314.5 million, although the segment result declined by EUR 10.9 million to EUR 70.4 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Finland-Sweden revenue fell EUR 3.3 million to EUR 225.5 million, with the segment result decreasing to EUR 1.3 million, partly reflecting 68 days of vessel maintenance.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Estonia-Sweden revenue declined EUR 12.1 million to EUR 85.3 million, while its loss narrowed to EUR 1.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Restaurant and shop sales, nearly half of total revenue, decreased to EUR 366.4 million from EUR 376.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Cargo transportation revenue fell to EUR 77.9 million from EUR 88.6 million, and charter revenue declined to EUR 54.9 million from EUR 62.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Personnel expenses increased 4.3% to EUR 201.0 million, while fuel and emission costs were broadly stable at EUR 96.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Depreciation and amortisation fell EUR 18.0 million to EUR 79.8 million, primarily because vessel useful lives were extended to 45 years and three vessels were sold.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Net finance costs also declined to EUR 21.4 million from EUR 28.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The Group sold Star I, Regal Star and Sailor and ended the year with no vessels in lay-up.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Operating cash flow remained positive at EUR 127.1 million, although below EUR 153.4 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Proceeds from vessel disposals contributed EUR 78.8 million to investing cash flow.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Interest-bearing liabilities declined 19.9% to EUR 445.9 million and net debt to EUR 432.4 million, while the equity ratio improved to 56.4%.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Cash and cash equivalents were EUR 13.5 million, supplemented by EUR 96.9 million of unused overdraft facilities.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: A dividend of EUR 0.06 per share, totalling EUR 44.6 million, was paid, and the same dividend is proposed for 2026.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, and K6 are all PRESENT with clear coverage in the candidate summary. K7 (capital investments) is MISSING—no mention of EUR 33.0 million investments or vessel-days. K8 (emissions reduction strategy) is MISSING—no reference to biomethane transition or GHG targets. K9 (management changes) is MISSING—no mention of board resignations/appointments. The summary captures most HIGH and MEDIUM core elements except for three MEDIUM items, resulting in a Generally yes rating (score 3).
